title: Ingrown toenail removal
what: With local numbing, the doctor removes the edge of the nail that has grown into the skin. Usually only a strip is removed, not the whole nail.
why: When the edge of the nail cuts into the skin of the toe and causes pain, inflammation, or pus, and home care does not help.
tell_doctor: Blood vessel problems in the legs, or poor circulation

prepare.title: Feet
prepare.text: Wash your feet before the visit. Remove nail polish.

prepare.title: Shoes
prepare.text: Bring roomy shoes or open slippers. There will be a dressing on the toe.

prepare.title: Getting home
prepare.text: Your toe will be numb, which makes driving awkward. It is better if someone else takes you home.

bring: Your referral, if you have one
steps: You lie down or sit, and your foot is cleaned
Numbing injections are given at the base of the toe
You wait a few minutes for the toe to go numb
The doctor separates and removes the ingrown edge of the nail
Often the growth area of that edge is treated so it does not grow in again
feel: The numbing injections hurt. This is the most unpleasant part
After that you feel nothing in the toe, only touch
When the numbing wears off, the toe aches. A painkiller your doctor suggests will help
after: For the first day, keep your foot raised
Change the dressing as the doctor says, usually after 1 to 2 days
Later, cut your nails straight across, without rounding the corners
red_flags: Pain and swelling get worse, or the redness spreads
Pus, a bad smell, or a fever

faq.q: Will the nail grow in again?
faq.a: Sometimes it does. To prevent this, the doctor often treats the growth area of the nail edge.

faq.q: Can an ingrown toenail be treated without surgery?
faq.a: In mild cases, foot soaks, correct nail cutting, and nail braces help. If there is pus or the pain does not go away, you need a doctor.
Only the numbing injections hurt. You will not feel the procedure itself.
